export_controls.text:
🚨 Trump’s corruption is a national security threat.

The President of the United States bought millions in NVIDIA stock, then approved advanced AI chip sales to China.

He’s sacrificing America’s technological edge and cashing in doing it. https://t.co/MVa0ji4zg9

deepseek.reason: The speaker criticizes approved AI chip sales to China as sacrificing US technological edge, supporting restrictions.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement directly condemns approval of advanced AI chip sales to China.

export_controls.text:
Trump should not be selling our advanced AI chips to China.
 
He’s giving the advantage to an adversary, and I want to know why.
 
@RepGregoryMeeks and I demanded answers with @HouseForeign last week, and we'll keep up the drumbeat.

https://t.co/UzczvAkcnT

deepseek.reason: The speaker says Trump should not sell advanced AI chips to China, supporting export restrictions.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement directly opposes the chip sales with clear national-security reasoning.

export_controls.text:
Trump is handing our opponents our coordinates in the middle of a battle by selling China high-powered AI chips.

It puts our national security at risk.

But don't take it from me, take it from the experts who testified in front of @HouseForeign. https://t.co/M37AD9PTnD

deepseek.reason: The speaker condemns selling high-powered AI chips to China as a national-security risk, implying support for restricting such exports.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement clearly criticizes a specific chip sale to China as dangerous, though it does not name a bill.

export_controls.text: Right now, our laws do not explicitly cover the remote access of technologies via network connections, including the internet or cloud computing services. H.R. 2683 would close this gap by giving the Bureau of Industry and Security statutory authority to control the remote access of items by bad actors who aim to jeopardize our national security or foreign policy interests.
export_controls.context: House floor speech in support of H.R. 2683, the Remote Access Security Act, during debate on the bill.

deepseek.reason: The speaker endorses H.R. 2683 to give BIS authority over remote access, closing an export-control gap.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly supports extending export controls to remote/cloud access, though it does not name AI.

china_race_dynamics.text:
In our @Sciencedems hearing today, I discussed how investing in domestic research is key to beating China in the AI innovation race. 

Unfortunately, the Trump administration seems to be rowing in the wrong direction. 

By canceling STEM research grants to fund AI training and deporting international students, Trump is threatening our country’s ability to compete.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says domestic research investment is key to beating China in the AI innovation race and criticizes actions that threaten U.S. competitiveness.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly endorses competing with China in the AI innovation race.
